correctness.summary: Same defect as SpatialKeyedMap: ValidatePosition only checks `math.any(quantized >= this.QuantizeWidth)` and omits the lower bound (quantized < 0). The map is an UnsafePartialKeyedMap whose Update→RecalculateBuckets indexes buckets directly via `Buckets[key]` with key range [0, quantizeSize*quantizeSize); CheckAllKeysOutOfBounds is only compiled under collections checks. A position below -halfSize yields a negative quantized coordinate, a negative hash, and an out-of-bounds heap write in release builds.
correctness.triggeringInput:
new LocalSpatialMap

(quantizeStep:1, size:4) built over a position Position=(-3f,-3f): quantized=floor((-1,-1))=(-1,-1); validation any((-1,-1) >= 4) is false → passes; Hash = -1 + (-1)*4 = -5; UnsafePartialKeyedMap.RecalculateBuckets executes Buckets[-5] (OOB write).
correctness.rootCause: ValidatePosition checks only the high side of the world bounds; negative quantized coordinates (positions below -halfSize) are not rejected and become negative bucket indices into a directly-indexed bucket array.
correctness.suggestedFix: Add the lower-bound check: `if (math.any(quantized < int2.zero) || math.any(quantized >= this.QuantizeWidth))` before computing/using the hash.

perf.summary: Eliminate the redundant modulo on the tail worker by assigning end = Positions.Length directly.
perf.currentCost: Positions.Length % Workers is an extra integer division (~20-40 cycles on ARM) executed on the last worker's Execute.
perf.proposedChange: Replace the if (index == Workers-1) { end += Positions.Length % Workers; } block with end = (index == Workers-1) ? Positions.Length : end; (or compute end as Positions.Length on the last worker), removing the % division.
perf.rationale: start + length + (Length % Workers) on the last worker algebraically equals Positions.Length, so the modulo result is redundant. Removes a division from the per-Execute setup.
perf.risk: Exact for Workers>=1, guaranteed by math.max(1, JobWorkerCount) at the call site.
